prompt: What is a downside of using reflection compared to direct code?
choices: Reflection only works with public classes
Reflection bypasses compile-time type checking, is slower, and makes code harder to understand and refactor
Reflected method calls cannot throw exceptions
explanation: Reflection loses type safety (errors become runtime, not compile-time), has performance overhead (method lookup each time), and makes code harder to follow in IDEs. Use it as a last resort when direct code or generics won't work.
